page: Vultr vbm-24c-384gb-amd is a dedicated bare metal server configured for high memory capacity and sustained multi-threaded compute. Built on the x86_64 architecture, the server features a 24-core, 48-thread AMD EPYC 9254 processor operating at a base clock speed of 2.9 GHz. It includes 32 KB of L1 data cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster, with hardware support for AVX-512 vector instructions, AES cryptography, and AMD SVM virtualization extensions. The platform includes 384 GB of DDR5 system memory clocked at 6 GHz, providing 8.0 GB of RAM per physical thread.

Storage consists of a bundled 960 GB local SSD without discrete GPU accelerators. In synthetic and application benchmarks, the system posts top-tier single-core and multi-core results, registering 2,272 in Geekbench single-core and 21,196 in Geekbench multi-core tests. High memory bandwidth is demonstrated by uncached read throughput reaching 296.64 GB/sec and write throughput reaching 164.02 GB/sec. Database and in-memory key-value benchmarks show robust throughput, with Redis recording 72.25 million set operations per second.

With its 8:1 RAM-to-vCPU ratio and high memory bandwidth, the server is architecturally suited for in-memory databases, memory-bound caching tiers, container orchestration nodes, and continuous integration workloads requiring substantial compilation and decompression throughput. Local storage capacity remains modest at 960 GB, making external storage attachments necessary for data sets exceeding onboard solid-state boundaries.
description: Vultr vbm-24c-384gb-amd is a dedicated bare metal instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9254 processor with 24 physical cores and 48 vCPUs clocked at 2.9 GHz. The server pairs compute resources with 384 GB of high-speed 6 GHz DDR5 memory, yielding an 8 GB per vCPU allocation, and includes a 960 GB local SSD. It does not include dedicated graphics processing units. Synthetic evaluations position the platform in the top tier for Geekbench single-core and multi-core execution, supported by AVX-512 vector extensions and uncached memory read bandwidth measuring 296.64 GB/sec. It delivers high throughput in memory-bound operations, including 72.25 million Redis set operations per second. The server offers a solid profile for in-memory caching tiers, large-scale enterprise databases, software build pipelines, and containerization hosts where RAM density and dedicated core execution are essential.
